theory.intro: A **continuous uniform distribution** spreads probability evenly across an interval $[a,b]$, where $a<b$, so its density is the constant $f(x)=\frac{1}{b-a}$. Every probability is then the area of a rectangle.
facts: $f(x)=\frac{1}{b-a}$ for $a\le x\le b$, and $f(x)=0$ for every other value of $x$.
For $a\le c\le d\le b$, $P(c\le X\le d)=\frac{d-c}{b-a}$, the width of the interval divided by the width of the whole support.

For any requested interval $[c,d]$ with $c\le d$, use the length of its intersection with $[a,b]$, divided by $b-a$. An interval running outside $[a,b]$ is cut back to the boundary, because $f(x)=0$ outside the support; a disjoint interval has probability $0$.
steps: Find the width of the support, $b-a$.
Multiply the density by the length of the part of the requested interval within the support; if there is no overlap, the probability is $0$.

workedExamples.question_text: The continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on $[3,11]$. Find its probability density function and explain why its total area is $1$.

$X$ is uniformly distributed on $[-2,10]$. Find:
a. $P(1\le X\le5)$
b. $P(X\le4)$
c. $P(X>7)$.

A machine produces a cord length $X$, in centimetres, uniformly distributed on $[120,132]$. Find:
a. $P(128\le X\le136)$
b. $P(115\le X\le123)$
c. $P(134\le X\le138)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The density is $\frac{1}{132-120}=\frac{1}{12}$ on $[120,132]$ and $0$ outside it. Use only the part of each requested interval within the support.

a. The overlapping interval is $[128,132]$.
$\begin{align*}P(128\le X\le136)&=\frac{1}{12}(132-128)\\&=\frac{1}{3}.\end{align*}$

b. The overlapping interval is $[120,123]$.
$\begin{align*}P(115\le X\le123)&=\frac{1}{12}(123-120)\\&=\frac{1}{4}.\end{align*}$

c. The interval $[134,138]$ has no overlap with $[120,132]$.
$P(134\le X\le138)=0$.

foundation.question_text: $X$ is uniformly distributed on $[3,15]$. Find $P(5\le X\le 9)$.

$X$ is uniformly distributed on $[1.25,7.75]$. Find $P(2.5\le X\le 5.25)$.
